event.asset: TMS (including accelerated protocols) for major depressive disorder
event.title: APA depression guideline lists TMS as a first-line treatment
event.proposition: The American Psychiatric Association issues a practice guideline for major depressive disorder that lists TMS (including accelerated protocols) as a first-line treatment option.
event.criterion: TRUE on the publication date of an American Psychiatric Association practice guideline, or guideline update, for major depressive disorder that recommends TMS (any protocol, including accelerated protocols) or another non-ECT neuromodulation modality as a first-line treatment option, that is, as an initial treatment not conditioned on prior antidepressant failure. A draft for comment, a payer policy, or a recommendation limited to treatment-resistant depression is not adoption. Resolution source: APA Practice Guidelines (psychiatryonline.org).
readings: 'Neuromodulation (especially accelerated TMS)' resolves on TMS; another non-ECT neuromodulation modality listed as first-line for MDD also counts.
ECT does not count: its existing role in severe or psychotic depression is not the change the claim describes.

'First-line treatment for depression' means the guideline lists the modality as an initial treatment option for MDD without requiring prior antidepressant failure; a listing only for treatment-resistant depression does not count.

records.stage_note: At the statement date TMS is recommended for depression after antidepressant failure (a later-line option), not as an initial treatment. No base-rate class covers a guideline reclassification; abstain.
